annotation.title_clean: Criminal Law Regulation of Robotics: Results of a Sociological Study
annotation.title_en: Criminal Law Regulation of Robotics: Results of a Sociological Study
annotation.summary_en: Journal article reporting an online survey of 305 Russian legal professionals and students on criminal law regulation of robotics. It covers the definition of a robot, awareness of regulation, risks, unauthorized access to robot software (Articles 272–273 of the Criminal Code) and criminal liability for harm by autonomous robots. It supports the author's earlier proposals for criminal law reform.
key_provisions_or_claims: Survey of 305 respondents (legal scholars, practitioners, students, law enforcement) in Russia, May–June 2021.
71.1% define a robot as a hardware-software device capable of physical manipulation and information processing.
60.9% are unaware of any legal acts regulating robots.
97% see risks of unauthorized access to robot software; 83.6% consider it a crime.
Supports supplementing Articles 272 and 273 of the Russian Criminal Code and developing criminal liability for harm by autonomous robots.
